memory_candidates.content: When a repository-owned script must serialize its own `lake build` (or similar) calls against a build guard that lives in a disposable, regenerated deploy tree (.claude/), take an flock() on the SAME lock path the guard publishes in its own header as a stable convention, rather than probing for or calling the guard binary. Advisory locks are keyed on the filesystem path, not the process that opened them, so the script and the guard exclude each other with zero coupling: no detection logic, no hardcoded reference into the deploy tree, unchanged behavior in a clone with no agent system deployed. A further useful trick: if the lock's file descriptor is opened early and deliberately never explicitly released (no `flock -u`), it stays held until the script process exits, so every LATER .lake-reading step in the same script run inherits the same protection for free, with no additional lock code -- provided those later steps are gated by the same precondition (e.g. the same RUN_BUILD flag) as the first locked step, which should be confirmed by grepping every build-launching call site in the file rather than assumed.

Never run a bare `git stash` (or `git stash pop`) on a shared working tree while concurrent sibling agents are dispatched against it in the same /orchestrate cycle. `git stash` with no pathspec stashes the ENTIRE working tree, including siblings' uncommitted work in unrelated task directories and shared files (TODO.md, state.json, events.jsonl). A `stash pop` can then conflict with a sibling's fresh edit made while the stash was held, stranding everything -- including your own work -- in the stash. If a single file's pre-edit baseline needs to be captured, use a read-only `git show HEAD:<path>` or `git diff <path>` instead. If recovery from an already-created stash is needed, extract only the paths this task owns via `git show stash@{N}:<path> > <path>` (a plain file write, not `git checkout stash@{N} -- <path>`, which the repo's destructive-git guard hook blocks on any dirty tree) -- never a blanket pop/apply on a shared tree.
